findings.title: `firstName` returns the LAST name, not the first name
findings.body:
The function claims to return "the person's first name" but `split(" ")[1]` returns the **second** word, which is the last name in "First Last" format.

**Evidence:**
- Input: "Ada Lovelace" → Output: "Lovelace" (should be "Ada")
- Input: "John Smith" → Output: "Smith" (should be "John")

The correct implementation should use `split(" ")[0]` to get the first word.
findings.verified: Confirmed by tracing the code: `name.trim().split(" ")` on "Ada Lovelace" returns ["Ada", "Lovelace"], so index [1] is "Lovelace" (the last name).

findings.title: `firstName` crashes on single-word names
findings.body: When given a single name like "Ada", `split(" ")[1]` is `undefined`, causing "Welcome back, undefined!"

findings.title: `firstName` crashes on empty or whitespace-only strings
findings.body: For empty strings or strings with only spaces, `name.trim().split(" ")[1]` is `undefined`.

findings.title: `firstName` returns empty string with multiple spaces between names
findings.body: "Ada   Lovelace".split(" ") produces ["Ada", "", "", "Lovelace"], so [1] is "" (empty string), resulting in "Welcome back, !"

findings.title: `firstName` crashes with leading/trailing whitespace on single names
findings.body: " Jane ".trim() is "Jane", then split(" ") gives ["Jane"], so [1] is undefined.
